title: Proper direct image on the localizing categories
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. An admissible coefficient $\Lambda$ is a finite commutative ring $A$ annihilated by a power of $\ell$, or one of $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb$ [sk-def-localizing-closure]; use the condensed coefficient conventions, in particular the finite-subextension convention for $\Qlb$ [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Write $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ for the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category, $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ for its bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ for their replete triangulated closure under all small ambient direct sums [sk-def-localizing-closure], and $Rp_*$ for the total right derived module-object pushforward [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Let $p:X\to Y$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Suppose $Rp_*$ maps $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ and preserves direct sums of objects of $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$. Then $Rp_*$ restricts to an exact (triangulated), sum-preserving functor $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$ [def-weil-triangulated-category].

For the following coefficient assertions, work in the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $k$ is a field of characteristic $r>0$ different from $\ell$, $X,Y$ are separated and of finite type over $k$, and $p$ is a proper $k$-morphism. Both hypotheses above hold for $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$, for finite $\Lambda=A$, and for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$. The cases $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $\mathbf Z_\ell$ are included by taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$.

proof.text: The module-object pushforward $p_*$ is additive by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and $Rp_*$ is its total right derived functor computed on K-injectives by [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Hence [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] makes $Rp_*$ exact on the ambient unbounded derived categories. Put $\mathcal L_X=\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ and $\mathcal L_Y=\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$, and let $\mathcal S$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal L_X$ on objects $K$ with $Rp_*K\in\mathcal L_Y$. By [sk-def-localizing-closure], both $\mathcal L_X,\mathcal L_Y$ are replete triangulated subcategories closed under small ambient sums. Exactness implies $Rp_*0\simeq0$, commutation with shifts, and preservation of distinguished triangles, so $\mathcal S$ contains zero, is replete, is closed under both shifts, and contains the third vertex of a distinguished triangle whenever it contains the other two. It contains $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ by the first hypothesis. For a small family $(K_s)$ in $\mathcal S$, its ambient sum lies in $\mathcal L_X$, and the second hypothesis gives $Rp_*(\bigoplus_sK_s)\simeq\bigoplus_sRp_*K_s\in\mathcal L_Y$. Thus $\mathcal S$ is itself a localizing subcategory of the ambient source containing the generators. Minimality in [sk-def-localizing-closure] gives $\mathcal L_X\subseteq\mathcal S$; the reverse inclusion is its definition. The restriction is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-restriction]. Its sums are the ambient sums: maps from the ambient coproduct to any object of the full subcategory have the same universal property there. Thus the assumed ambient sum comparison also proves sum preservation of the restricted functor. No sum preservation outside $\mathcal L_X$ was used. For the Lean size conventions, [lem-grothendieck-derived-has-coproducts] supplies ambient coproducts indexed in the Hom universe. The source closure is closed under those coproducts by lifting the indexing type and then reindexing. To cover larger existing coproducts, their nonzero summands inject into the endomorphisms of their coproduct by projection-inclusion idempotents, and hence form a Hom-universe small set. Reindex to that set, apply preservation there, and reinsert the zero summands. Thus the asserted preservation covers the original indexing universe without assuming unavailable large ambient coproducts.

source.place: First paragraph: restricted-sum localizing argument; ambient exactness and restriction made explicit.

proof.text: For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, the standing schemes $X,Y$ are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], applied to their separated finite-type structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Apply [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] to each: $\Dctf=\Dbc$ and their localizing closures agree. Clause (2) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational] now gives preservation of $\Dctf$ by $Rp_*$. Clause (3) of [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums] puts $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$ inside $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$. For every small family in that localizing closure, [sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window-ii] therefore gives precisely the ambient direct-sum comparison required in Step 1. Both hypotheses follow, so Step 1 supplies the exact sum-preserving restriction in these two cases.

source.place: Second paragraph, rational coefficient case: bounded constructibility, equality with Dctf, and sums on Dic.

proof.text: For a finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring $A$, clause (1) of [det-ctf-finite-proper-localizing] gives $Rp_*\Dctf(X,A)\subseteq\Dctf(Y,A)$ and an exact sum-preserving restriction on the localizing closures. Because these closures are full and closed under ambient sums, their coproducts are ambient coproducts, so its sum comparison is exactly the second hypothesis of Step 1. Both hypotheses hold for finite $A$. No equality $\Dctf=\Dbc$ is needed or asserted for a nonregular finite ring.

source.place: Second paragraph, final sentence: finite coefficient case quoted there; expanded using the existing finite localizing theorem.

proof.text: For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] again makes $X,Y$ qcqs, so [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] identifies $\Dctf$ with $\Dbc$ on both schemes and identifies their localizing closures. Clause (1) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-integral] sends $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ into $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, giving the first hypothesis. Properness includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $Y$ is quasi-compact; thus [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] supplies a uniform integer $d\ge0$ bounding the dimensions of all fibres of $p$. Clause (3) of [det-prop-int-compactness-direct-sums] applies with this bound and gives sum preservation on $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$, hence on $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E))$. These are ambient sums by fullness and ambient sum closure, as in Step 1. This is the second hypothesis, and Step 1 proves the integral restriction. Setting $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ in this step and Step 2 gives the $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $\mathbf Q_\ell$ cases respectively.

source.place: Second paragraph, final sentence: integral case quoted there; explicit bounded-constructible preservation and fibre-bound hypothesis.

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs; finite and integral cases expanded according to the unit first proof paragraph. Step 1 now records the proved generic coproduct-existence tool and the elementary nonzero-support size argument used by the Lean proof (B4, 2026-10-19); steps 2--4 remain open.

statement_correction.old_statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be admissible and $p\colon X\to Y$ proper. Suppose that $Rp_*$ maps $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into
$\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ and preserves direct sums of objects of $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$. Then $Rp_*$ restricts to an
exact, sum-preserving functor $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$. The hypotheses hold:

- for $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$, by [sk-thm-sfb-proper-base-change] and [sk-lem-proper-unbounded-window-ii] (sums in
  $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\subset\Dic(X,\Lambda)$);
- for $\Lambda=A$ finite, by [sk-prop-ctf-finite-proper];
- for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, by [sk-prop-int-compactness], using $\Dctf=\Dbc$.
statement_correction.reason: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the coefficient claims omitted the standing scheme setting required by rational/integral proper base change and by the qcqs Dctf=Dbc identification. Type-check failure: a general proper morphism does not give qcqs source/target or standing schemes (identity of an infinite disjoint union of Spec(k) is proper). Spell out the source intended sk-def-sfb-dc-setting only for the coefficient claims; keep the generic conditional assertion unchanged.
